## From Methodology to Procedure

**Methodology** answers: What will you study and why?

**Procedure** answers: How exactly will you do it?

# Procedure Development {background-color="#275882"}

## Step by Step (~30 min)

---

## What is a Procedure?

A procedure is a detailed, **replicable** description of what happens from the moment a participant arrives until they leave.

::: {.callout-tip}
## The Test

Could someone who has never seen your study run it identically from your procedure alone?
:::

---

## Procedure Template

| Phase | What Happens | Time |
|-------|--------------|------|
| 1. Arrival | Greet participant, explain study | 2 min |
| 2. Consent | Participant reads and signs consent | 2 min |
| 3. Instructions | Explain task, check understanding | 2 min |
| 4. Condition 1 | [Describe what happens] | ? min |
| 5. Condition 2* | [If within-subjects] | ? min |
| 6. Measures | Complete questionnaire/test | ? min |
| 7. Debriefing | Explain purpose, answer questions | 3 min |

---

## Key Questions to Answer

::: {.exercise-box}
**Your procedure must specify:**

1. What does the participant do first?
2. What are the exact instructions given?
3. How long does each part take?
4. What does the experimenter do/say?
5. How is data recorded?
6. What happens if something goes wrong?
:::

---

## Activity: Draft Your Procedure

::: {.exercise-box}
**In your groups (20 minutes):**

1. List every step from arrival to departure
2. Estimate timing for each step
3. Note who does what (participant vs experimenter)
4. Identify any decision points or contingencies

**Write this on your procedure worksheet!**
:::

---

## Checkpoint 1

::: {.poll-box}
**Instructor Check:**

Circulate and verify:

- Every step is documented
- Timings are realistic (total under 30 min ideally)
- Both participant and experimenter actions are clear
- Nothing is ambiguous or left to interpretation
:::

---

# Materials & Instructions {background-color="#275882"}

## Creating Your Resources (~30 min)

---

## Types of Materials

Depending on your study, you may need:

| Material | Example |
|----------|---------|
| Stimuli | Images, sounds, videos, word lists |
| Questionnaires | Self-report measures, demographics |
| Data sheets | Recording forms for experimenter |
| Consent form | Information sheet and signature |
| Debriefing sheet | Explanation of true purpose |

---

## Standardised Instructions

::: {.definition-box}
**Standardised Instructions**: The exact words you say to every participant

Why standardise?

- Reduces experimenter effects
- Ensures consistency across testers
- Makes your study replicable
:::

---

## Writing Good Instructions

::: {.example-box}
**Poor**: "Do the memory task."

**Better**: "You will see a list of words. Try to remember them."

**Best**: "In a moment, you will see 10 words appear on the screen, one at a time. Each word will be shown for 3 seconds. Your task is to try to remember as many words as you can. After all 10 words have been shown, you will have 60 seconds to write down as many as you can remember. Please do not write anything until I tell you to begin. Do you have any questions?"
:::

---

## Activity: Create Instructions

::: {.exercise-box}
**In your groups (15 minutes):**

1. Write the exact instructions you will read to participants
2. Include instructions for EACH phase of your procedure
3. Write a comprehension check question

**Remember**: Write as if you are reading a script!
:::

---

## Materials Checklist

::: {.definition-box}
**Before your pilot, confirm you have:**

- [ ] Consent form (even a draft version)
- [ ] Standardised instructions (written out)
- [ ] All stimuli/materials ready (or clear plan to create)
- [ ] Data recording sheet
- [ ] Debriefing explanation
:::

---

## Checkpoint 2

::: {.poll-box}
**Instructor Check:**

Verify each group has:

- Written standardised instructions

:::

# Pilot Run {background-color="#275882"}

## Test Your Procedure (~30 min)

---

## Why Pilot?

::: {.callout-important}
## Every Study Needs Piloting

Piloting reveals:

- Confusing instructions
- Technical problems
- Timing issues
- Unexpected participant questions
- Missing materials
:::

---

## How to Pilot Today

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Roles:**

- One person acts as **experimenter**
- One person acts as **participant**
- Others **observe and take notes**

Rotate so everyone experiences both roles!
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
**Focus on:**

- Are instructions clear?
- Is the timing right?
- Does anything feel awkward?
- What questions might real participants ask?
:::
::::

---

## Pilot Feedback Form

| Issue | What Happened | How to Fix |
|-------|---------------|------------|
| Instructions unclear | Participant asked what "stimulus" meant | Change to "the picture" |
| Timing | Task took 8 min not 5 min | Reduce trials or extend procedure |
| Materials | Screen too small to read | Use larger font or different device |
| Flow | Awkward pause between sections | Add transition script |

---

## Activity: Run Your Pilot

::: {.exercise-box}
**In your groups (25 minutes):**

1. Assign roles (experimenter, participant, observers)
2. Run through your ENTIRE procedure
3. Observers note any issues on the feedback form
4. Rotate roles if time permits
5. Discuss improvements as a group
:::

---

## Checkpoint 3

::: {.poll-box}
**Instructor Check:**

After pilot runs:

- What worked well?
- What needs revision?
- Are there any fundamental problems?
:::

---

# Debrief & Troubleshooting {background-color="#275882"}

## Finalising Your Procedure (~20 min)

---

## Common Pilot Issues

| Issue | Solution |
|-------|----------|
| Instructions confusing | Simplify language, add examples |
| Takes too long | Cut non-essential elements |
| Participant got bored | Add variety, shorter tasks |
| Data not recording properly | Test technology in advance |
| Ethical concerns emerged | Revise consent/debriefing |

---

## Revise Your Procedure

::: {.exercise-box}
**Based on your pilot (10 minutes):**

1. List all issues identified
2. Decide on solutions for each
3. Update your procedure document
4. Note any materials that need revision
:::

---

## Debriefing Script

::: {.definition-box}
**Your debriefing should include:**

1. Thank participant for taking part
2. Explain the true purpose of the study
3. Explain any deception (if applicable)
4. Provide your contact details for questions
5. Remind them of right to withdraw data
:::

---

## Example Debriefing

::: {.example-box}
"Thank you for participating. This study was investigating whether background music affects memory performance. Half of participants completed the task with music, and half in silence. We predicted that music would impair memory due to cognitive load.

If you have any questions, please contact [name] at [email]. You may withdraw your data at any time before [date]. Thank you again for your contribution to this research."
:::

---
